units.name: Letters and Sounds
units.summary: The sounds letters make, and how they join to build words.

topics.name: Letter Sounds
topics.summary: Hearing the first sound in a word, and finding its letter.

objectives.text: Hear the first sound in a spoken word.
Name the letter that makes that sound.
Say the sounds in a short word and join them together.

keyTerms.definition: A mark we write, like a, b or c.
What you hear when you say a letter out loud.
Sounds joined together that mean something, like cat.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
Letters have sounds.

You will learn to hear the first sound in a word.

You will learn to join sounds to make a word.

sections.heading: A letter has a name and a sound
sections.body:
The letter m has a name. We call it "em".

But it makes a different noise: mmmmm.

That noise is its SOUND.

When you read, you use the sound, not the name.

Try these. Say the sound out loud:

    m  says  mmmm
    s  says  sssss
    t  says  t
    a  says  a  (like in cat)

sections.heading: The first sound
sections.body:
Say this word slowly: mmmmat.

What did you hear first?

You heard mmmm.

That is the letter m.

So mat begins with m.

Try it with your own name. Say it slowly. What sound comes first?
sections.example:
Finding the first sound in sun.

Say it slowly. Stretch the beginning:

    sssssun

The first sound is sss.

Which letter says sss?

The letter s.

So sun begins with s.

Now try pot. Say it slowly: p-ot. The first sound is p. So pot begins with p.

sections.heading: Joining sounds to read a word
sections.body:
A short word is just a few sounds stuck together.

Take the word cat. It has three sounds:

    c ... a ... t

Say them one at a time. Slowly.

Now say them faster. And faster.

    c-a-t ... cat

You read the word.

That is all reading is. Sounds, joined up.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.body:
Say every word out loud. Slowly first.

1. What is the first sound in map?

2. What is the first sound in ten?

3. Join these sounds and say the word: s ... i ... t

4. Join these sounds and say the word: p ... e ... n

5. Say your own name slowly. What is the first sound?

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body:
• A letter has a name and a sound.
• When you read, you use the sound.
• Say a word slowly to hear its first sound.
• Join the sounds together and you have read the word.

questions.question: Say the word "map" slowly. What sound do you hear FIRST?
questions.explanation: Stretch the beginning: mmmmap. The first sound is mmm, which is the letter m. If you chose p, that is the sound at the END of the word, not the beginning.

questions.question: Join these sounds together: s ... i ... t. What is the word?
questions.explanation: Say them faster and faster: s-i-t, sit. Keep the sounds in the order they are given. "its" has the same letters but in a different order, so it is a different word.

questions.question: Which word begins with the same sound as "sun"?
questions.explanation: Sun begins with sss. Say each choice slowly. Sit also begins with sss. Ten begins with t, cup with c, man with m. Only sit matches.
